lesson: The 7/8 mechanism and the anticausal Hankel block read opposite ends of the off-line pole set: 7/8 bounds the largest real part (growth of the causal prime-side kernel, a half-plane device that is height-uniform), while the summed anticausal trace reads the smallest real part and the index is a count that no growth exponent sees. Family sums of bridges are either a direct sum or the bridge of the product; neither couples members, and for a positive quadratic quantity orthogonality keeps the diagonal. For unimodular twists n^{-i alpha} a family sum is literally a height average, so family bounds on the index are densities.
